AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the general municipal law, in relation to allowing alcoholic beverages as prizes in any game of chance
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S940

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to allowing
alcoholic beverages as prizes in any game of chance

 PURPOSE :

The purpose of this bill is to allow bona fide charitable
organizations participating in games of chance such as raffles, etc.,
to offer alcoholic beverages as a prize.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Sections 1: Strikes the last line of section 195-d of the general
municipal law that states "No alcoholic beverage shall be offered or
given as a prize in any game of chance".

Section 2: Creates restrictions for raffles that award prizes
containing alcohol.

Section 3: Sets the effective date immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This legislation looks to cut unnecessary, over burdensome and
outdated bureaucracy around prizes offered for charitable gaming,
while promoting charitable donations and helping nonprofits with their
fundraising activities.

Currently, New York State Law prohibits charitable organizations
participating in a game of chance to raffle off prizes that contain
alcohol. Though State Law outlaws this action, most charitable gaming
organizations do not know this is illegal and partake in the activity
as a form of common practice. It is common for a local winery,
brewery, or beverage distributor to donate a basket of their products
to a charitable organization to help raise money for the cause the
charitable organization supports.

The prohibition on alcohol as a prize came about in 1976, when the
laws around charitable gaming first came into existence due to a
constitutional amendment that the voters approved in the 1975 general
election (Article I, S9) - which permits localities to authorize,
subject to state legislative supervision and control, the conduce of
games of chance events.

According to the 10-day budget report of this legislation in 1976, the
voter referendum on games of chance came about because games of chance
operations were being conducted by charitable and service
organizations on a widespread and open basis, although such games were
illegal.

This legislation looks to make changes to the laws of 1976 for similar
reasons, with raffling off alcohol as a common, widespread practice
although such activity is illegal. This new legislation will clarify
confusion within the beverage industry and charitable gaming groups,
while accelerating the growth of craft beverages, beer, wine and
spirits industries and bona fide charitable and service organizations.
Craft breweries, wineries and distilleries often donate products to
charities as in-kind donations, as a way to help the charity while at
the same time, promoting their products. We should not be restricting
the growth of one of New York's fastest growing industries. Wineries,
cideries and brewery businesses in New York State have showed
consistent and significant growth over the last few years and are

putting themselves at legal-risk when they donate their products to
charities as in-kind donations for raffle purposes.

According to the New York State Brewers Association, the number of New
York State breweries grew from 95 in 2012 to 207 in 2014, making them
3rd in the country with an Economic Impact of $3.5 Billion dollars.
In 2012, New York State was the 6th largest beer producing state
behind California, Pennsylvania, Colorado, Ohio and Oregon. New York
State craft breweries increased production by 26% from 557,436 in 2011
to 859,536 barrels in 2012, while at the same time nationally, the
craft beer segment only grew by 15%.

According to the New York Wine and Grape Foundation, the New York
grape, grape juice and wine industry generates more than $4.8 billion
in economic benefits annually for New York State. New York is home to
over 1,600 family vineyards and over 400 wineries, producing more than
175,000,000 bottles of wine per year while providing $408 million in
state and local taxes.

While the local beverage industry is growing, charitable gaming
revenue has remained stagnant. Groups that participate in charitable
gaming are authorized organizations, defined as any bona fide
religious, charitable, educational, service, veteran or volunteer fire
organization which operates without profit to its members. These
organizations foster and support worthy causes and undertakings that
the majority of the electorate support. The raffles they host are one
of the many fundraising techniques the organizations use. Raffling off
donated products helps promote the product itself, while providing the
charitable organization one-hundred percent profit - a win for both
the charity and business.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.6265/A.8623 of 2016; Passed Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
